A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Simple Policy Optimization work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained experiments across substantial redrawing and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Atari learning curves, KL-divergence and policy-entropy measurements, and over-optimization experiments in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original Atari experiments, including PPO-variant comparisons, network-depth tests and threshold-sensitivity results in Sections 4.1–4.4 and Appendices B–E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the advantage-sign-dependent, KL-clipped SPO objective are unchanged (v1 Equation 9; v2 Equation 12). v2 expands their explanation and evaluates deeper networks without introducing a new SPO component or optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B covers the same 35 Atari games in both versions. Added analyses use already represented games; Riverraid, newly included in the 1,000-epoch stress-test figure, was already evaluated elsewhere. Transformers, diffusion models and LLMs are proposed applications, not additional evaluated domains.

E2.justification: v1's main learning-curve comparison uses standard PPO-CLIP. v2 Figure 3 adds PPO-PENALTY and PPO-CLIP with early stopping, providing direct comparisons against alternative KL-control mechanisms. PPO-C denotes the original PPO baseline; Appendix B retains the two-method comparison, and SO remains in Figure 1.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled shallow/deep-network comparisons, matches the new PPO variants' KL thresholds to SPO's 0.02, and summarizes sensitivity-study returns over the last 10% of training. The existing 1,000-epoch stress test expands from three to four games. Default training remains 10 million steps with eight update epochs.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and Appendices D–E add network-depth robustness tests and full-training threshold sensitivity analyses covering return, KL divergence and entropy. These extend beyond v1's over-optimization sweeps. v1's 100-epoch Figures 4–5 are removed, while Figure 1 and the expanded 1,000-epoch analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random-seed runs with standard deviations for the main Atari experiments and five seeds in Figure 1. v2's additional sensitivity error bars do not introduce a stated change in run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds return, KL and entropy results for PPO variants, deeper networks and full-training threshold sweeps. New findings include substantial PPO learning degradation with deeper networks on Breakout and DemonAttack. Figure 1 also replaces several gradually increasing Amidar KL curves with rapidly plateauing trajectories despite retaining the 100-epoch, five-seed caption.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 change from L >= J minus a penalty to eta >= L minus a penalty, reversing the return–surrogate relation. v2 removes v1's SPO-specific conditional bound, Equation 13, and reverses the KL arguments in the PPO-PENALTY formula. These materially revise the formal justification.

C1.justification: v1's abstract says SPO sometimes outperforms PPO. v2 claims better sample efficiency against mainstream PPO variants, higher policy entropy and robustness to network depth or complexity. Network robustness becomes an explicit introduction contribution, substantially broadening the retained first-order KL-clipping proposal's claims.

C2.justification: v2 introduces KL–entropy and exploration explanations, distinguishes SPO from early stopping, and extrapolates the depth results to Transformers, diffusion models and possible RLHF applications. Section 3 also softens ensuring better monotonic improvement to potentially achieving it, replacing v1's more definite interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly specifies convolution channels, kernels, strides and shallow/deep fully connected layer dimensions; v1 supplied only a generic network description. Table 1 adds settings for the new PPO baselines, including 0.02 KL thresholds. Existing default hyperparameters, preprocessing information and the code-access link remain.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning against KL-control alternatives, adding discussion of early stopping and citations including Achiam, Sun et al. and Chen et al. It also introduces substantial application-oriented positioning around Transformers, diffusion models and RLHF/DPO, with corresponding references absent from v1.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, substantially expands Section 3 into a stepwise explanation of the unchanged objective, and restructures the experimental narrative into four parts. The discussion is expanded and dedicated appendix sections organize the new comparisons, sensitivity analyses and architecture documentation.

P2.justification: Main figures are recomposed into multipart return/KL/entropy displays, with new depth and sensitivity plots and an architecture schematic. Appendix B's retained plots are redrawn with changed colors, axes and omitted legends. Table 1 expands from two to four methods, constituting extensive visual revision.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's important comparison gap by testing SPO against PPO variants specifically designed to control KL divergence. Controlled depth and sensitivity studies, revised bounds and explicit network diagrams substantially strengthen validation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the unexplained Figure 1 curve replacement and the speculative mechanism and large-model extrapolations.
